title: Positive products and radii of convergence
statement:
Let $\{f_j(t)\}_{j\in J}$ be a locally finite family of series

$$
f_j(t)=1+\sum_{n\ge1}a_{j,n}t^n\in1+t\mathbf R_{\ge0}[[t]],
$$

meaning that each coefficient of the formal product
$F(t):=\prod_{j\in J}f_j(t)=\sum_{n\ge0}A_nt^n$ receives contributions
from only finitely many factors. If this formal series is the Taylor
series at $0$ of a function holomorphic on $|t|<R$, then every
$f_j$ has radius of convergence at least $R$ (in the sense of [d-real-series]). In particular, if
$f_j=P_j(t)^{-1}$ with $P_j(0)=1$ a polynomial, then $P_j$ has no
zero in $|t|<R$.

proof.text: Fix a factor j and a degree n. Choose the finite set S in the local finiteness hypothesis. Products of the factors have nonnegative coefficients by induction using the antidiagonal formula for multiplication, and constant coefficient one. If j is in S, write the product as f_j times the product over S\{j}; the antidiagonal term (n,0) is a_{j,n}, and all other terms are nonnegative. If j is absent and n>0, local finiteness forces a_{j,n}=0. At degree zero both constant coefficients are one. Thus 0 ≤ a_{j,n} ≤ A_n, and all A_n are nonnegative, in the conventions of [d-real-series].

Let $h$ be the function in the hypothesis, with Taylor coefficients $A_n=h^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For each real $0\le t<R$, apply [lem-rp-taylor-sum-on-disc] at $c=0$ and $z=t$ to obtain summability of $\sum_n A_nt^n$ in $\mathbf C$. Taking real parts gives summability of the same real series; its terms are nonnegative by step 1. The hypotheses needed by the cited result are exactly holomorphy on $|z|<R$ and $|t|<R$; no regularity on the boundary $|z|=R$ is used.

source.place: ## Proof, analytic convergence input replacing the Cauchy coefficient estimate

proof.text: By [d-real-series], nonnegative complex coefficients have norm equal to their real part, so step 2 gives summability of ∑ ‖A_n‖ t^n. The proved source-library PowerSeries.le_radius_of_summable and ENNReal.le_of_forall_nnreal_lt give R ≤ radius(F), including R=0 and R=∞. The coefficient inequalities in step 1 give ‖a_{j,n}‖ ≤ ‖A_n‖. Apply the proved PowerSeries.radius_le_radius_of_norm_coeff_le, whose proof uses [lem-rp-nonnegative-summable-comparison], to get radius(F) ≤ radius(f_j). Compose the inequalities.

source.place: ## Proof, radius comparison and passage to R

proof.text: For f_j=P⁻¹ and P(0)=1, the constant coefficient of P is nonzero. Apply the already proved PowerSeries.eval_ne_zero_of_lt_radius_inv from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Analysis.Analytic.ConvergenceRadius. A point z in the disc of radius R has ‖z‖ < R ≤ radius(f_j)=radius(P⁻¹) by step 3. The cited theorem evaluates the absolutely convergent Cauchy product P P⁻¹=1 at z; if P(z)=0 this would give 0=1. This implements the unit route that a zero cannot cancel the numerator one.

source.place: Final sentence: a zero of the polynomial is a pole of its reciprocal.

proof_origin.place: Coefficient domination and radius comparison; Taylor convergence replaces Cauchy estimates, and the proved source-library inverse-polynomial theorem supplies the no-cancellation conclusion by an absolutely convergent Cauchy product.

The statement and proof are identical in both snapshots; the item's statement is unchanged and not weakened. Step 1: a finite subset S from local finiteness gives 0<=a_{j,n}<=A_n by the coefficient expansion; elementary and correct. Step 2: Complex.hasSum_taylorSeries_on_eball (TaylorSeries.lean:87; CompleteSpace, DifferentiableOn on eball, z in eball, r in ENNReal) applied at c=0, z=t in [0,R); the terms are real, so the series is summable in R. Step 3: Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (ENNReal.lean:530) with u=a_{j,n}t^n, v=A_nt^n; R itself is then admissible in the sup of d-real-series, so R(f_j)>=R, including R=0 and R=infinity. Step 4: double-sum identity 1=sum_k p_k z^k s_{N-k}(z) for N>=d, checked. Step 5: subtracting P(z)s_N gives 1 <= finitely many tails of the convergent sum b_n|z|^n, which tend to 0; contradiction, checked. The steps realize unit step 1 (domination, radius definition) and unit step 2 (a zero cannot cancel the numerator 1); route kept, no tool_uses needed. Both leaves are exact or one-line Mathlib specializations, self-contained, not clauses of the item. A scan of all DAG statements and mathlib_match fields found no duplicates. Small cases tested: (1-t)^{-1}(1-2t)^{-1} with R=1/2; the counterexample 1+t times (1+t)^{-1} shows the nonnegativity hypothesis is necessary. No SGA. lean.statement: theorem positive_product_radius {J : Type u} (f : J → ℂ⟦X⟧) (hf : ∀ j, (f j).HasNonnegCoeffs) (hconst : ∀ j, PowerSeries.constantCoeff (f j) = 1) (F : ℂ⟦X⟧) (hlocal : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ S : Finset J, (∀ (j : J) (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → k ≤ n → PowerSeries.coeff k (f j) ≠ 0 → j ∈ S) ∧ PowerSeries.coeff n F = PowerSeries.coeff n (∏ j ∈ S, f j)) (R : ℝ≥0∞) (h : ℂ → ℂ) (hh : DifferentiableOn ℂ h (Metric.eball 0 R)) (hTaylor : ∀ n : ℕ, PowerSeries.coeff n F = (Nat.factorial n : ℂ)⁻¹ * iteratedDeriv n h 0) : (∀ j : J, R ≤ (f j).radius) ∧ (∀ (j : J) (P : Polynomial ℂ), f j = (P : ℂ⟦X⟧)⁻¹ → P.eval 0 = 1 → ∀ z ∈ Metric.eball 0 R, P.eval z ≠ 0)
